content.text: The web composer resolves @mentions into ADF mention nodes. The CLI deliberately does not, so the agent path — the primary path — silently drops the notification.
- cmd/gadak/agent.go:1255-1257 says so in a comment: "No mention resolution: `@Name` in a CLI body stays plain text and notifies nobody." It calls jira.Doc(body, nil).
- The web path passes a mentions map (internal/server/write.go:503-528).

- Live mirror: of 24047 comments, 17579 contain a real ADF mention node and 17660 contain a literal '@' in text. Three quarters of the comments already written are proper mentions; only the agent-authored ones are not.
- The feed's mention tab keys on ADF type=mention with attrs.id (internal/server/feed.go:624-658), so a CLI mention never appears there either.
Why it is a defect and not a missing feature: the user writes "@Dana" and the tool accepts it, reports success, and Dana is never told. Nothing in the output says the mention was inert.

Fix shape: the CLI resolves mentions the way the server already does — SearchUsers, take a single hit, and on zero or multiple hits exit non-zero printing the candidates (the failure shape `gadak transition` already uses for an ambiguous name). No new local user store; SearchUsers is an origin call. issuetap already preserves mention nodes on POST, so there is no standalone work.
Gate: FAIL-first is that the serialized body today contains no "type":"mention". After: a single hit produces the node; an ambiguous name is refused with candidates.
This is the mention half of GDK-21. The edit/delete half stays where it is; this half is a defect and should not wait behind it.
Found by the Jira-surface gap sweep (track B, score 10/10).
